<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The .SRCINFO file is standard AUR package metadata describing the onionspray package. The source URL points to https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/onion-services/onionspray.git#tag=v1.8.1, which is the official Tor Project GitLab repository for this tool — the expected upstream source. The pinned tag (v1.8.1) is used rather than a mutable branch, which is good practice. The sha256sums = SKIP is standard and required for VCS sources. All declared dependencies (perl, bash, tor, openbsd-netcat, rsync, openssl) and optional dependencies are consistent with a tool for setting up Onion Services. No suspicious network destinations, obfuscated commands, or unexpected file operations are present in this metadata file.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches the declared OnionSpray upstream repository from the Tor Project GitLab at a version tag and packages it. Use of `sha256sums=('SKIP')` for a VCS source is standard and not evidence of malicious behavior.

`git submodule update --init --recursive` fetches upstream-declared submodules at build time; this is normal for projects with submodules, though it reduces reproducibility if submodule refs are mutable. The package copies the source tree, including `.git`, to `/opt/onionspray`; this is unusual hygiene-wise because VCS metadata is shipped, but it is not itself malicious. The wrapper disables upstream `update`/`upgrade` commands and delegates updates to pacman.

No exfiltration, credential theft, reverse shell, unrelated downloads, encoded/obfuscated commands, or execution of downloaded code is present. The `sed` change suppresses a `chmod` failure for non-root help invocations; this may weaken fail-closed behavior around secret directory permissions, but does not by itself constitute a supply-chain attack.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Declared upstream packaging; no malicious behavior found.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
